title: DC Chinatown Restaurant Guide
guide_order_note: Places are in print-guide order: the six featured restaurants first (Lucky Danger #1 through Chinatown Garden #6), then the remaining 16 by cuisine section as they appear in the booklet (Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese, Taiwanese, Poke, Bubble tea, Bakery & desserts, Bar). Rank numbers match the numbered pins on the map.

walk_origin.name: Walter E. Washington Convention Center south facade (801 Mount Vernon Place NW)
walk_origin.method: Manhattan distance on the street grid from the south edge of the Convention Center OSM footprint (bbox min lat 38.90313), 3 mph walking pace, times rounded to the nearest minute.

basemap_attribution: © OpenStreetMap contributors (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright). The map is a custom SVG street grid drawn from OpenStreetMap ways, not raster tiles.

cuisine_sections.intro: The heart of the old Chinatown: Cantonese roast meats and noodle shops on H and 6th Streets, plus newer hand-pulled noodle, Sichuan and soup dumpling spots.
Ramen, izakaya plates, fried chicken and conveyor sushi, including the Daikaya group's two spots at 6th and G.
Two pho spots facing each other across the 600 block of H Street.
Taiwanese fried chicken, at a Luna Hall counter it shares with Kung Fu Tea.
Build-your-own poke bowls inside Luna Hall.
Bubble tea also turns up at Reren and Joy Luck House.
A Korean-French bakery café inside Luna Hall.
Luna Hall's own bar, in the food hall's lounge.

places.name: Lucky Danger
places.hours: Tue–Thu 11:30 a.m.–2 p.m. and 4:30–9 p.m.; Fri 11:30 a.m.–2 p.m. and 4:30–10 p.m.; Sat 4:30–10 p.m.; closed Sun–Mon
places.hours_source: Official site, luckydanger.co/washington-dc, fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.group_notes: Mahjong room bookable by the hour; private classes for up to 15
places.location: 7th and D St NW, three blocks south of the Chinatown boundary.
places.blurb: Tim Ma's love letter to American Chinese takeout has traveled a long way: a 2020 pandemic pop-up, an Arlington takeout spot from 2021 and, since June 2025, this full-service flagship. Executive chef Robbie Reyes treats the canon (General Tso's chicken, beef and broccoli, crab rangoon) as something worth reworking, not apologizing for. Come for the cocktail bars; stay for the back mahjong room and its three automatic shuffling tables, billed as DC's only public one.

places.name: Ambrosia
places.hours: Mon–Thu 10 a.m.–1 a.m.; Fri–Sun 10 a.m.–2 a.m.
places.hours_source: PoPville, Sep 1, 2026, quoting the restaurant; Ambrosia’s own site returned HTTP 503 on Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: Modern Vietnamese (pho, banh mi, wok dishes, cocktails) now fills the old Tony Cheng's space, a quiet changing of the guard on H Street. It opened in late August 2026 and keeps night-owl hours: 1 a.m. on weeknights, 2 a.m. Friday to Sunday.

places.name: Wok and Roll
places.hours: Mon–Tue 11 a.m.–9:30 p.m.; Wed 11 a.m.–1 a.m.; Thu–Sat 11 a.m.–2 a.m.; Sun 11 a.m.–1 a.m.
places.hours_source: DowntownDC BID listing, downtowndc.org/explore/places/wok-and-roll-restaurant-karaoke/, fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.group_notes: Private karaoke rooms (karaoke hours differ; see wokandrolldc.com/daily-hours)
places.blurb: Chinese and Japanese plates, sushi included, share the bill with private karaoke rooms you can book for a group. The building has a past: 604 H St is the historic Surratt boarding house.

places.name: Joy Luck House
places.hours: Tue–Sun 10:30 a.m.–8:30 p.m.; closed Mon
places.hours_source: Official site joyluckhouse.com (hours) and Restaurantji listing updated Nov 15, 2026 (closed Monday)
places.blurb: A small bakery-café where the glass case does the talking: warm egg tarts and mooncakes, chased with homemade iced tea or taro boba. It does breakfast, too.

places.name: Reren Lamen & Bar
places.hours: Daily 11:30 a.m.–10 p.m.
places.hours_source: Official site rerenlamen.com/contact/ and DowntownDC BID listing, both fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: The headline is hand-pulled lamen (la mian) in layered broths. Around it: Chengdu spicy wontons, xiao long bao, handmade dumplings, and a full bar that also pours bubble tea. A second location holds down Georgetown.

places.name: Chinatown Garden
places.hours: Daily 11 a.m.–9 p.m.
places.hours_source: Restaurant ordering site chinatowngardenwashington.com, as listed Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: A long-running Cantonese and Hong Kong-style room on H Street that turned toward a more traditional Chinese menu in 2015, betting on its roots rather than chasing trends.

places.name: Chinatown Express
places.hours: Daily 11 a.m.–10 p.m.
places.hours_source: Current listings (including Tripadvisor) as of Nov 26, 2026; official info page was not reachable
places.blurb: The show starts in the front window on 6th Street, where noodles are pulled by hand in full view. The order is the roast duck noodle soup, which Washington Post readers named a must-try in 2013; Cantonese roast meats, shrimp wonton noodle soup and beef chow foon fill out a menu that knows exactly what it is.

places.name: New Big Wong
places.hours: Mon–Fri 4:30 p.m.–2 a.m. (Fri until 3 a.m.); Sat 4 p.m.–3 a.m.; Sun 4 p.m.–2 a.m.
places.hours_source: Google business listing, checked Nov 26, 2026; Apple Maps also shows a 4:30 p.m. opening. Closing times match Destination DC's late-night list (Aug 2026). The DowntownDC BID previously listed a 10:30 a.m. opening.
places.blurb: A lower-level Cantonese dining room (meat, seafood and vegetarian dishes, done the traditional way) with a reputation for outlasting the night: it stays open until 2 a.m. Sunday to Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday and Saturday.

places.name: China Boy
places.hours: Mon, Wed–Sun 9:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Tue
places.hours_source: Restaurantji and Eater DC venue listing, as of Nov 26, 2026; official ordering site did not return a usable page to this refresh
places.blurb: A Cantonese counter whose house-made rice noodles are the whole point; dry-fried beef chow fun is how they're known. Daytime only: roughly 9:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed Tuesdays.

places.name: Cinnara
places.cuisine_detail: Chinese (Southwest Chinese beef noodles, individual hot pots)
places.hours: Daily 11 a.m.–9:30 p.m.
places.hours_source: Official site eatcinnara.com, fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: Formerly Bonkers' Chinese Burger, this 6th Street counter has turned toward Southwest China as a noodle and hot pot shop. Everything hinges on a slow-simmered beef bone broth, the base for its signature beef noodles (Mala Spicy Beef Noodle Soup and Taiwan Braised Beef Noodle Soup among them). Individual hot pots draw on Sichuan, Chongqing, Guizhou and Yunnan flavors; handmade dumplings, pork wontons and fresh fruit teas round it out. Open daily, 11 AM to 9:30 PM.

places.name: Dumpling District
places.cuisine_detail: Chinese (soup dumplings, Shanghainese dim sum, noodles)
places.hours: Sun–Thu 11 a.m.–10 p.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–11 p.m.
places.hours_source: Tous les Jours official store-hours widget for Luna Hall DC and consistent hall listings, Nov 26, 2026
places.location: Inside Luna Hall, 625 H St NW.
places.blurb: Luna Hall's anchor, and the reason many people walk in: soup dumplings (xiao long bao) in pork, chicken, mala spicy pork, crab and pork, shrimp and zucchini, and black truffle. Can't choose? The Rainbow Soup Dumplings platter settles it with one of each. Beyond the steamer: pan-fried bao, potstickers, pork wontons in chili oil, scallion pancakes, fried rice, stir-fried noodles and noodle soups.

places.name: Kung Fu Tea
places.cuisine_detail: Bubble tea (milk, fruit and classic teas)
places.hours: Sun–Thu 11 a.m.–10 p.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–11 p.m.
places.hours_source: Same as Luna Hall; Yelp lists a combined Kung Fu Tea / TKK stall at 625 H St, Nov 26, 2026
places.location: Inside Luna Hall, 625 H St NW.
places.blurb: The Kung Fu Tea chain's Luna Hall branch, where tea, milk and fruit drinks are the starting point and the toppings (bubbles, beans, jellies, pudding) are where you make it yours. It's open 11 AM to 9:30 PM.

sources.label: Kung Fu Tea DC store list

places.map_listing_note: Google lists Kung Fu Tea and TKK Chicken as one counter.

places.name: TKK Fried Chicken
places.hours: Sun–Thu 11 a.m.–10 p.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–11 p.m.
places.hours_source: Same as Luna Hall; confirmed still at the DC hall via Yelp (Kung Fu Tea / TKK) and current listings, Nov 26, 2026. TKK’s national site did not list this address.
places.location: Inside Luna Hall, 625 H St NW.
places.blurb: TKK has been frying chicken since 1974, when its first shop opened in Taipei's Ximending. Here it comes as mixed buckets, sandwiches or tenders, in original, crispy mild or crispy spicy, with curly fries alongside. The Infatuation (Nov 2023) scored it 8.5 and pointed straight at the tenders. It shares a counter with Kung Fu Tea.

sources.label: Yelp (Kung Fu Tea / TKK Fried Chicken)

places.map_listing_note: Shares its Google and Apple Maps listings with Kung Fu Tea (same counter).

places.name: Poke Ninja
places.hours: Sun–Thu 11 a.m.–10 p.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–11 p.m.
places.hours_source: Luna Hall Group site still lists Poke Ninja at the DC hall; hours same as the hall, Nov 26, 2026
places.location: Inside Luna Hall, 625 H St NW.
places.blurb: Build-your-own poke in the familiar steps (size, base, proteins, toppings, crunch, sauce), or let a signature bowl decide: the Ninja Blaze stacks salmon, ahi tuna, jalapeño, cherry tomato, sriracha and spicy mayo; the Shuriken Sensation pairs ahi and spicy tuna with mango and avocado.
places.map_listing_note: No separate map listing; links go to Luna Hall.

places.name: Tous les Jours
places.hours: Sun–Thu 11 a.m.–10 p.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–11 p.m.
places.hours_source: Official store page tljus.com/stores/washington-dc-625-h-st-nw hours widget, fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: The Korean bakery-café chain's Luna Hall outpost at Unit 101, part of the hall's lineup since July 2024. Breads, cakes, pastries and breakfast sandwiches line up beside specialty coffee, smoothies and teas. Hours run 11:15 AM to 10:30 PM.

places.name: Luna Bar
places.cuisine_detail: Cocktail bar in the food hall
places.hours: Sun–Thu 11 a.m.–10 p.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–11 p.m.
places.hours_source: Same as Luna Hall, Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: Luna Hall's own bar: a lounge of comfy seats, upbeat music, DJ gear, lights and a fully stocked bar, bookable for events. The practical move is to grab a drink here while you wait on a TKK order.
places.map_listing_note: No separate map listing; links go to Luna Hall.

places.name: Daikaya Ramen Shop
places.hours: Mon–Thu 11:30 a.m.–9:30 p.m.; Fri 11:30 a.m.–10:30 p.m.; Sat 11 a.m.–10:30 p.m.; Sun 11 a.m.–9:30 p.m. Walk-in only.
places.hours_source: Official hours page daikaya.com/location/daikaya-dine-in-hours/, fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: The first floor does one thing: traditional Sapporo-style ramen. No reservations, no detours.

places.name: The Izakaya at Daikaya
places.hours: Tue–Thu 5–9:30 p.m.; Fri–Sat 5–10:30 p.m.; Sun 5–9 p.m.; closed Mon
places.hours_source: Official location page daikaya.com/location/daikaya/, fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: Upstairs, Daikaya becomes a Japanese tavern: creative small plates, craft cocktails, a rare Japanese whisky collection and DJs on weekends. Book on OpenTable, and don't come up here expecting ramen.
places.map_listing_note: Google lists Daikaya's two floors as one place; Apple lists the Izakaya separately.

places.name: Bantam King
places.hours: Mon–Fri 11:30 a.m.–2:30 p.m. and 5–9 p.m.; Sat–Sun 11 a.m.–9 p.m.
places.hours_source: Official location page bantamking.com/location/bantam-king/, fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: The Daikaya team's ode to the bird, in chicken ramen and fried chicken. The chicken is halal-certified from Noor Al-Jabal, and happy hour runs weekdays, 5 to 7 p.m.

places.name: Kura Revolving Sushi Bar
places.hours_source: Official location page (Mon–Wed, Sat–Sun) plus Restaurantji weekly hours updated Nov 11, 2026 (Thu–Fri). On Nov 26 the official page showed Thursday closed and Friday 11:30 a.m.–9 p.m., matching its posted Thanksgiving/Black Friday hours, not the regular week.
places.blurb: Sushi circles past on a conveyor belt at this national chain; udon, ramen and desserts fill in the gaps.

places.name: PHO 88 Noodles & Grill
places.hours: Mon–Sat 11 a.m.–10 p.m.; Sun noon–9 p.m.
places.hours_source: Official site pho88dc.com and DowntownDC BID listing, both fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: Pho leads a lineup of Vietnamese noodle soups, backed by broken rice plates, rolls and Vietnamese coffee.

places.name: Sharetea DC Chinatown
places.hours_source: Official contact page shareteadcchinatown.com/contact-us/, fetched Nov 26, 2026
places.blurb: A local franchise of the Taiwanese bubble tea chain, steps from the corner of 5th and H Streets.

listings_check_note: Google and Apple Maps listings, official websites and Instagram accounts were checked for all 22 places on November 26, 2026 (Thanksgiving Day, so 'today' hours on some listings were holiday hours; regular weekly hours were compared).
